Why do we call Krishna Govinda? It wasn't his birth name. As the story goes, after Krishna held up Govardhan for seven days, Indra, the king of rain, finally understood. He came down from the sky, ashamed.
But he didn't come alone. Behind him walked Surabhi, the mother of all cows. She looked at the little boy who had protected every cow in Vraj.
Wait, what did she do? She poured her milk over him, like a waterfall, and bathed him. Then Indra bowed and gave him a new name. Govinda. The protector of cows.
That's why, even today, when we sing Govinda, we are thanking the boy who protected the cows. Comment Govinda, and share this with someone who loves cows.
